description: We are an ambitious team from Madinah in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, working on "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts".
summary:
Idea: An AI companion for astronauts that eases isolation and depression on long missions, while monitoring their health and stepping in when needed. Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, which asks teams to “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions.”

The problem:

Astronauts are isolated, confined, and far from home.
Signals take time to reach Earth (~1.3 seconds to the Moon, up to ~22 minutes to Mars).
Current solutions rely on pre-recorded conversations and a generic, non-personalized AI personality.

The solution:

A companion built around the astronaut’s own preferences, with a human-like conversational style.
It reads data from bio-monitors and steps in proactively when vital signs drop.
It runs offline (Edge AI) and refreshes news and conversation topics through DTN (Delay/Disruption-Tolerant Networking).
It logs interactions in a timeline for future research.

NASA resources:

Human Research Program (HRP) datasets and the Lunar Health Monitor, used to set validated health intervention thresholds.
IMCA and Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) frameworks, used for autonomous offline syncing and decision support.

Impact:

Space: Stronger psychological resilience and earlier health intervention.
Earth: Support for isolated workers, such as polar stations and offshore sites.
Feasibility: Built on technology available today: Edge AI, wearable bio-monitors, and offline DTN architecture
details:
What it does and how it works
Mission Companion is an AI companion for astronauts on space missions. It combines health monitoring with emotional support. It reads data from wearable bio-monitors and holds personalized, human-like conversations built around each astronaut’s own preferences. When vital signs drop, it steps in proactively. It runs offline (Edge AI) and refreshes news and conversation topics through Delay/Disruption-Tolerant Networking (DTN). Every interaction is logged in a timeline for future research.

Benefits

  • Reduces the effects of isolation and depression.
  • Provides early health intervention when vital signs drop.
  • Replaces pre-recorded conversations and generic AI personalities with a personalized companion.
  • Supports future research through the interaction timeline.

Intended impact

  • In space: Enhances psychological resilience and early health intervention.
  • On Earth: Supports isolated workers.

Tools, data and technology

  • Human Research Program (HRP) datasets and the Lunar Health Monitor, used to set health intervention thresholds based on proven space research standards.
  • IMCA and Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) frameworks, used for autonomous, reliable offline syncing and decision support.
  • Edge AI, wearable bio-monitors, and DTN architecture.

How it is creative
Existing solutions rely on pre-recorded conversations and a non-personalized AI personality. Mission Companion is a personalized, human-like companion built on the astronaut’s own preferences, and it works offline.

Factors the team considered

  • Isolation and depression on long missions.
  • Delayed communication with Earth, and the need for offline support.
  • Health intervention thresholds based on NASA research.
  • Feasibility using Edge AI, wearable bio-monitors, and DTN.
